news.headline: Aug. 27: Flash Flooding Overwhelms Nepal, and Jury Deliberates in Lindsay Clancy’s Murder Trial
news.body: Devastating flash floods and mudslides wreaked havoc along the Nepal-China border this week, leaving hundreds dead and more than 1,000 missing. More than 500 foreigners are among the missing, including, by one estimate, roughly 65 Americans. NBC News correspondent Janis Mackey Frayer explains why the destruction happened without warning and what role climate change may have played. Then, jury deliberations are underway in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who killed her three young children. While Clancy doesn’t dispute the killings, her defense team is arguing that she shouldn’t be held criminally responsible because she was experiencing postpartum psychosis. But the prosecution insists she acted intentionally and deliberately. As the jury weighs a set of complex outcomes, NBC News legal analyst Misty Marris breaks down what evidence and testimony from the five-week trial could be key to reaching a verdict. Finally, 2026 could be the year of the foldable phone. Samsung and Google already have models on the market, and Apple is reportedly planning to drop its version in September. But are consumers willing to shell out $2,000 for a little extra screen? NBC News chief tech analyst Joanna Stern explains why the phones have appeal.

Initial USGS estimates of 8.0 were downgraded, and aftershocks were reported.

A deep earthquake struck near Japan's Bonin Islands on October 25, with magnitudes reported between 6.5 and 7.0 and a depth of approximately 470–500 km. Cyclone Arnab has intensified over the Bay of Bengal and is expected to make landfall near the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28, with sustained winds reaching up to 140 km/h, classified as a very severe cyclonic storm. Heavy rainfall is anticipated in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, prompting authorities to prepare for large-scale evacuations.
Andhra Pradesh is preparing to evacuate approximately 5.7 lakh people from vulnerable areas, and schools in Odisha have been closed as Cyclone Arnab approaches. West Bengal and other eastern states are on alert, with authorities coordinating response measures. The India Meteorological Department has issued specific district‑level warnings.

There have been no immediate reports of injuries or damage resulting from the earthquake.
